title: Work & Professions
subtitle: Talk about jobs, office life, and finding work in French

lessons.title: Les métiers
lessons.description: Name dozens of professions and switch between masculine and feminine forms.

blocks.heading: Saying what someone does
blocks.body: To give a profession, French uses «être» plus the job — and drops the article. You say «Je suis médecin», never «Je suis un médecin». The article comes back only when you add a describing word, as in «C'est un bon médecin». The question you will hear most often is «Qu'est-ce que vous faites dans la vie ?»

examples.french: Qu'est-ce que vous faites dans la vie ?
examples.english: What do you do for a living?

examples.french: Je suis infirmier dans un hôpital.
examples.english: I am a nurse in a hospital.

examples.french: Elle est architecte à Bordeaux.
examples.english: She is an architect in Bordeaux.

examples.french: Mon père est boulanger depuis vingt ans.
examples.english: My father has been a baker for twenty years.

examples.french: C'est une très bonne journaliste.
examples.english: She is a very good journalist.

blocks.tip: «Tu fais quoi dans la vie ?» is the relaxed version you will hear between friends.

blocks.heading: Where you work
blocks.body: Add a place with «dans» (in) or «chez» (at a company, at someone's business). Use «pour» when you name the employer. These three little words let you turn a bare job title into a real sentence.

examples.french: Je travaille dans une école primaire.
examples.english: I work in a primary school.

examples.french: Il travaille chez Renault depuis trois ans.
examples.english: He has worked at Renault for three years.

examples.english: We work for a small company.

examples.french: Elle travaille à domicile le vendredi.
examples.english: She works from home on Fridays.

examples.french: Mon frère travaille en usine.
examples.english: My brother works in a factory.

blocks.heading: Talking about a job you like
blocks.body: To describe the work itself, French speakers use «un métier» with an adjective: passionnant (exciting), utile (useful), difficile (hard), bien payé (well paid). The verb «exercer» is the slightly formal way to say you practise a profession.

examples.french: C'est un métier passionnant mais fatigant.
examples.english: It's an exciting but tiring job.

examples.french: J'adore mon métier, je rencontre beaucoup de gens.
examples.english: I love my job, I meet a lot of people.

examples.french: Elle exerce ce métier depuis dix ans.
examples.english: She has practised this profession for ten years.

examples.french: Ce n'est pas très bien payé, mais c'est utile.
examples.english: It isn't very well paid, but it's useful.

examples.french: Je voudrais changer de métier.
examples.english: I would like to change careers.

blocks.tip: «Un métier» suggests a trade you have learned; «un travail» is the work itself and «un emploi» is the paid position.

blocks.heading: Masculine and feminine job names
blocks.body: Most professions have two forms. The four patterns below cover almost everything: add -e, change -er to -ère, change -eur to -euse, change -teur to -trice. Some jobs ending in -e (journaliste, architecte, comptable) never change — only the article does.

examples.french: un avocat → une avocate
examples.english: a lawyer (m) → a lawyer (f)

examples.french: un boulanger → une boulangère
examples.english: a baker (m) → a baker (f)

examples.french: un coiffeur → une coiffeuse
examples.english: a hairdresser (m) → a hairdresser (f)

examples.french: un instituteur → une institutrice
examples.english: a teacher (m) → a teacher (f)

examples.french: un journaliste → une journaliste
examples.english: a journalist (m) → a journalist (f)

examples.french: un informaticien → une informaticienne
examples.english: an IT specialist (m) → (f)

blocks.tip: Newer feminine forms like «une professeure», «une ingénieure» and «une pompière» are now standard in France, Belgium and Canada.

blocks.heading: No article after être
blocks.body: After «être», a profession stands alone with no «un» or «une». The article only comes back with «c'est» or when an adjective describes the person.

examples.english: I am a teacher.

examples.english: He is an excellent cook.

examples.english: My neighbour is a police officer.

examples.english: She is a well-known lawyer.

lessons.title: Au bureau
lessons.description: Describe your office, your daily tasks, and how long you have been doing them.

blocks.heading: A day at the office
blocks.body: The French working day has its own rhythm: you «arrivez au bureau», you «allumez l'ordinateur», you «répondez aux courriels», and around eleven o'clock there is «la pause-café». Meetings are «des réunions», and the day ends when you «quittez le bureau».

examples.french: J'arrive au bureau à neuf heures.
examples.english: I arrive at the office at nine.

examples.french: Je réponds à mes courriels le matin.
examples.english: I answer my emails in the morning.

examples.french: On fait une pause-café vers onze heures.
examples.english: We take a coffee break around eleven.

examples.french: J'ai une réunion avec mon chef à quatorze heures.
examples.english: I have a meeting with my manager at 2 p.m.

examples.french: Je quitte le bureau vers dix-huit heures.
examples.english: I leave the office around six.

blocks.tip: «Le bureau» means both the desk and the office — context tells you which one.

blocks.heading: Talking about your tasks
blocks.body: Use «je dois» (I have to) and «je m'occupe de» (I take care of) to explain your responsibilities. «Une tâche» is a task and «un dossier» is a file or a case you are handling.

examples.french: Je dois terminer ce dossier avant vendredi.
examples.english: I have to finish this file before Friday.

examples.french: Je m'occupe des clients étrangers.
examples.english: I take care of the foreign clients.

examples.french: J'ai beaucoup de tâches aujourd'hui.
examples.english: I have a lot of tasks today.

examples.french: Peux-tu imprimer ce document, s'il te plaît ?
examples.english: Can you print this document, please?

examples.french: Je suis débordé cette semaine.
examples.english: I'm swamped this week.

blocks.heading: Working from home
blocks.body: «Le télétravail» (remote work) is now very common in France. People say «je télétravaille» or «je travaille à distance». Flexible hours are «des horaires flexibles», and the fixed schedule is «le planning».

examples.french: Je fais du télétravail deux jours par semaine.
examples.english: I work remotely two days a week.

examples.french: Nos horaires sont assez flexibles.
examples.english: Our hours are quite flexible.

examples.french: La réunion est en ligne à dix heures.
examples.english: The meeting is online at ten.

examples.french: Le planning de la semaine est sur l'écran.
examples.english: The week's schedule is on the screen.

examples.french: Mon collègue travaille à distance depuis Lyon.
examples.english: My colleague works remotely from Lyon.

blocks.tip: In an office email, «Cordialement» is the safe, neutral sign-off — the French equivalent of «Best regards».

blocks.heading: depuis, pendant, il y a
blocks.body: These three words all translate as "for" or "ago", but they answer different questions. «Depuis» = the action started in the past and is STILL going on — French uses the present tense here, where English uses "have been -ing". «Pendant» = a finished period, usually with the passé composé. «Il y a» = how long ago something happened, always with a past tense.

examples.french: Je travaille ici depuis trois ans.
examples.english: I have been working here for three years.

examples.french: Je suis dans cette entreprise depuis 2022.
examples.english: I have been in this company since 2022.

examples.french: J'ai travaillé à Paris pendant deux ans.
examples.english: I worked in Paris for two years.

examples.french: J'ai changé de poste il y a six mois.
examples.english: I changed positions six months ago.

examples.french: Elle est en réunion depuis une heure.
examples.english: She has been in a meeting for an hour.

examples.french: Il a téléphoné il y a dix minutes.
examples.english: He called ten minutes ago.

blocks.tip: Quick test: if you can say "ago" in English, use «il y a». If the action is still happening now, use «depuis».

blocks.heading: Asking how long
blocks.body: To ask about duration, use «Depuis quand… ?» (since when) or «Depuis combien de temps… ?» (for how long). Both take the present tense in French.

examples.french: — Depuis six mois seulement.

examples.note: «ça fait… que» = another way to say depuis

lessons.title: Chercher un emploi
lessons.description: Read a job ad, write a simple CV, and handle the basics of a French interview.

blocks.heading: Reading a job ad
blocks.body: A French job ad («une offre d'emploi» or «une annonce») names «le poste» (the position), the contract («un CDD» for fixed-term, «un CDI» for permanent) and the profile wanted. «Nous recherchons…» means "we are looking for…" and «Profil recherché» introduces the requirements.

examples.french: Nous recherchons un vendeur à temps partiel.
examples.english: We are looking for a part-time salesperson.

examples.french: Le poste est à pourvoir en septembre.
examples.english: The position is available in September.

examples.french: Expérience de deux ans exigée.
examples.english: Two years of experience required.

examples.french: Envoyez votre CV et votre lettre de motivation.
examples.english: Send your CV and your cover letter.

examples.french: J'ai vu votre annonce sur Internet.
examples.english: I saw your ad on the internet.

blocks.tip: In France a CV is short — one page, no photo required, and always with dates for each job.

blocks.heading: Writing a simple CV
blocks.body: A French CV has four blocks: «Formation» (education), «Expérience professionnelle» (work experience), «Compétences» (skills) and «Langues» (languages). Each line starts with the dates, then the job title and the company.

examples.french: Formation : licence de gestion, université de Lille.
examples.english: Education: bachelor's degree in management, University of Lille.

examples.french: 2021–2024 : vendeuse chez Décathlon, Lyon.
examples.english: 2021–2024: salesperson at Décathlon, Lyon.

examples.french: Compétences : Excel, gestion d'équipe, service client.
examples.english: Skills: Excel, team management, customer service.

examples.french: Langues : français (langue maternelle), anglais courant.
examples.english: Languages: French (native), fluent English.

examples.french: J'ai fait un stage de six mois dans une banque.
examples.english: I did a six-month internship in a bank.

blocks.heading: In the interview
blocks.body: «L'entretien d'embauche» follows a predictable script. You will hear «Parlez-moi de vous», «Pourquoi ce poste ?» and «Quelles sont vos qualités ?». Answer with «Je suis…», «J'ai de l'expérience en…» and «Je suis disponible à partir de…».

examples.french: Parlez-moi un peu de vous.
examples.english: Tell me a little about yourself.

examples.french: J'ai trois ans d'expérience dans la vente.
examples.english: I have three years of experience in sales.

examples.french: Je suis sérieuse, organisée et motivée.
examples.english: I am serious, organised and motivated.

examples.french: Je suis disponible à partir du premier octobre.
examples.english: I am available from October 1st.

examples.french: Quelles sont vos prétentions salariales ?
examples.english: What salary are you looking for?

blocks.tip: Always end with «Je vous remercie de votre temps» and a handshake — French interviews stay formal, so use «vous» throughout.

blocks.heading: Being polite: je voudrais, j'aimerais, pourriez-vous
blocks.body: In a job application everything is softened. «Je veux» (I want) sounds blunt, so French uses the conditional: «je voudrais» or «j'aimerais» (I would like). To ask the recruiter for something, use «Pourriez-vous… ?» (Could you…?) or «Est-ce que je pourrais… ?» (Could I…?).

examples.french: Je voudrais poser ma candidature pour ce poste.
examples.english: I would like to apply for this position.

examples.french: J'aimerais travailler dans votre entreprise.
examples.english: I would like to work in your company.

examples.french: Pourriez-vous me donner plus d'informations ?
examples.english: Could you give me more information?

examples.french: Est-ce que je pourrais commencer en octobre ?
examples.english: Could I start in October?

examples.french: Je vous remercie de votre temps.
examples.english: Thank you for your time.

examples.french: Je reste à votre disposition.
examples.english: I remain at your disposal.
examples.note: standard closing line in a cover letter

blocks.tip: Never «tutoyer» a recruiter. Use «vous» from the first hello to the final handshake, even if the recruiter is your age.

blocks.heading: Talking about your past jobs
blocks.body: Use the passé composé for finished jobs («j'ai travaillé», «j'ai fait un stage») and the present with «depuis» for what you are still doing. Notice the verbs that take «être»: «je suis parti», «je suis resté».

examples.french: J'ai travaillé trois ans comme vendeuse.
examples.english: I worked as a salesperson for three years.

examples.french: J'ai fait un stage chez Airbus en 2023.
examples.english: I did an internship at Airbus in 2023.

examples.english: I stayed two years in that company.

examples.english: I have been working as a waitress since January.

passages.title: L'entretien de Sofia
passages.french:
Sofia a vu une annonce sur Internet : « Nous recherchons un assistant comptable, CDI, temps plein. »
Elle a envoyé son CV et sa lettre de motivation le soir même.
Trois jours plus tard, la recruteuse l'a appelée pour un entretien.
— Bonjour Sofia, parlez-moi un peu de vous.
— J'ai fait une formation en comptabilité à Toulouse et j'ai obtenu mon diplôme il y a deux ans. J'ai travaillé pendant dix-huit mois dans un petit cabinet.
— Quelles sont vos qualités ?
— Je suis sérieuse, organisée et je travaille bien en équipe.
— Parfait. Vous êtes disponible quand ?
— À partir du premier octobre.
Une semaine après, Sofia a signé son contrat.
passages.english:
Sofia saw an ad on the internet: "We are looking for an accounting assistant, permanent contract, full-time."
She sent her CV and her cover letter that same evening.
Three days later, the recruiter called her for an interview.
— Hello Sofia, tell me a little about yourself.
— I trained in accounting in Toulouse and I got my degree two years ago. I worked for eighteen months in a small firm.
— What are your strengths?
— I am serious, organised and I work well in a team.
— Perfect. When are you available?
— From October 1st.
A week later, Sofia signed her contract.
